preamble: De-retroflexion of the voiceless retroflex affricate [ʈʂ] to alveolar [ts] merges the retroflex and dental sibilant series. In colloquial Taiwanese Mandarin, Standard Mandarin zh- is pronounced as z- in most contexts. Most Southwestern Mandarin varieties, including Chengdu Sichuanese, merge zh, ch and sh with z, c and s, so Standard zhōng and zhēn correspond to Sichuanese zong1 and zen1. In Polish dialects with mazurzenie (Masovia, Masuria, most of Lesser Poland, parts of Silesia), standard cz [t͡ʂ] corresponds to c [t͡s]: czas [t͡ʂas] 'time' is cas [t͡sas]. Its origin is debated: Koneczna derives it directly from the 16th-century depalatalization of the older palato-alveolars /ʃ, ʒ, t͡ʃ, d͡ʒ/, which gave retroflexes elsewhere but dentals here, while Kuryłowicz argues that archaic dialects adopted the new retroflexes and replaced them with dentals. It is treated here as a synchronic dialect correspondence of standard Polish retroflex cz, sz, ż, dż [t͡ʂ ʂ ʐ d͡ʐ] to mazurating c, s, z, dz. Old Polish forms that entered the standard language with c, such as cudo for older czudo, are excluded because they predate the Polish retroflexes.

examples.note: Colloquial Taiwan Guoyu pronounces zh-, ch- and sh- like z-, c- and s- in most contexts.
The same merger applies to every zh- syllable.
Most Southwestern Mandarin varieties merge the retroflex series with the alveolar affricates and fricatives.

examples.from: Standard Mandarin 中 zhōng, 真 zhēn
examples.note: The correspondence is regular in Sichuanese Pinyin across zh- syllables.
Wiktionary labels cas Far Masovian, Przasnysz, Western Kraków and Zagórze; the Wikipedia Mazuration table gives the same pair.
Both the fricative and the affricate of szcz are fronted.

sources: Gogolewski, S. (2001). Dialectology in Poland, 1873–1997. In Koerner, E. F. K. & Szwedek, A. (eds.), Towards a History of Linguistics in Poland. John Benjamins. https://doi.org/10.1075/sihols.102.07gog
